topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets out the course structure, and outlines the learning objectives for the lecture on cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Genetic Mutations, Environmental Risk, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental concept of cancer as a disease driven by genetic mutations and microenvironmental factors, examining the interplay between intrinsic cellular bad luck, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Biological and Chemical Mechanisms of Carcinogens and Promoters
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the specific cellular and molecular mechanisms through which infectious agents, chemical mutagens, metabolic activation, chronic inflammation, tumor promotion, and host developmental timing contribute to cancer development.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the scientific methodologies used to establish carcinogenic risk, encompassing mutational signature analysis, population epidemiology, in vivo animal toxicology assays, and the in vitro Ames test.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary of environmental cancer risks and remarks on evaluating everyday benefit-to-risk trade-offs.
